title: PagerDuty INC-4821 checkout p99 latency
body:
Incident INC-4821 is open. Checkout p99 latency climbed to 2410 milliseconds starting 2026-09-12 18:04 UTC. The impact window is us-east-1 only. Error rate on the checkout-api is 3.2 percent 5xx. Severity is SEV-2. Status is investigating.

PagerDuty notes point at Redis checkout-pool saturation (49 of 50 connections) as the leading hypothesis. Promo-service fanout was also observed adding 400ms. No resolution ETA has been posted.

title: Statuspage payments-api degraded
body:
Payments-api is degraded as of 2026-09-12 20:40 UTC. We are seeing 12 percent 5xx on card-capture in us-east-1. Auth and refunds are not in the blast radius. A public status update was posted at 20:55 UTC.

Checkout page still renders. Tokenization retries are succeeding after one retry. The payments on-call is coordinating with the checkout incident INC-4821 but this is tracked as a separate component status.

title: Runbook checkout latency mitigation
body:
If checkout p99 exceeds 800 milliseconds for ten minutes, raise a SEV-2 and page checkout-primary. Confirm Redis checkout-pool utilization and checkout-api HPA current replicas before changing traffic.

Mitigation order: (1) raise checkout-api HPA max replicas from 12 to 20, (2) disable the promo-service fanout via the promo_attach flag, (3) increase Redis checkout-pool from 50 to 128 connections. Do not bounce Redis as a first step.

body:
Namespace checkout. Deployment checkout-api is 8 of 8 ready. HPA checkout-api-hpa is configured min 8 max 20. Current replicas are 12. Target CPU utilization is 65 percent. Observed CPU utilization is 71 percent.

Pod memory working set is 410Mi average. The snapshot omits container resource quantities. Last scale event was 2026-09-12 19:58 UTC scale-up from 10 to 12.

title: LaunchDarkly checkout_retry flag
body:
Feature flag checkout_retry is enabled at 15 percent canary in us-east-1. The flag adds one idempotent retry on checkout-api 5xx before returning to the client. Default off in every other region.

Targeting rules are user-key hash modulo 100 less than 15. Change history shows enablement at 2026-09-12 13:40 UTC by feature-store bot. This page records flag state only.

title: Datadog Redis checkout-pool saturation
body:
Redis checkout-pool connections are 49 of 50 in use (98 percent utilization) as of 2026-09-12 22:40 UTC. Pool wait time p99 is 180 milliseconds. Command latency p99 is 9 milliseconds, so the wait is connection acquisition, not Redis itself.

Evictions are zero. Memory is 1.1Gi of 2Gi. This chart is the live pool utilization, not a cache-eviction setting.

title: Security wiki password hygiene reminder
body:
Do not store production passwords in runbooks or Slack. Use the vault broker for service credentials. Shared spreadsheet passwords were retired in 2025.

This page is a hygiene reminder for humans handling credentials. It names no calendar or owner for credential refresh.

title: PagerDuty INC-3104 checkout latency (resolved)
body:
Incident INC-3104 was resolved on 2026-08-02. Checkout p99 had reached 1800 milliseconds after a bad promo-service deploy. Mitigation was a rollback of promo-service to 2026-08-01.18.

This write-up is historical. Do not use INC-3104 replica counts or pool sizes for current response. The 2026-08 playbook assumed HPA max 10, which is outdated.

title: Runbook Redis maxmemory-policy
body:
Redis checkout-cache maxmemory-policy is allkeys-lru. Maxmemory is 2gb. Apply with CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru on the primary, then persist in the helm values under redis.policy.

Last reviewed March 2026. If evictions climb above 1k/min, page cache-oncall. This is the only document that states the maxmemory-policy.

title: Runbook blue-green deploy procedure
body:
Blue-green deploy procedure for checkout-api: bake a green Deployment, shift 10 percent service traffic, watch error rate for 15 minutes, then flip the remainder. Keep blue scaled for 45 minutes.

This procedure was written for the 2026-Q1 ingress. The mesh cutover in April retired the blue-green switch described here. No replacement procedure is in this corpus.

title: Confluence auth token TTL
body:
Auth token TTL is 12 hours for user sessions and 90 minutes for service tokens. Refresh tokens last 14 days. These numbers were set during the November 2025 identity hardening week.

No later document in this corpus restates the auth token TTL. Treat this page as the only, and stale, source for TTL questions.

title: Runbook drain Kafka consumer lag on payments-worker
body:
To drain Kafka consumer lag on payments-worker, scale the consumer deployment to 16 pods and pause non-critical topics payments.audit and payments.email. Lag should fall under 5k messages in 20 minutes on the 2026-Q2 cluster.

The April 2026 broker set was decommissioned. This drain recipe is stale and must not be followed against the current cluster.
